newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity futures drop amid liquidation.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity futures drop amid liquidation.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures closed sharply lower amid continued long liquidation, trade sources said Friday.

"There has been a lot of largesse built into the market," said one trader. "Today we saw a continuation of longs giving up the ghost now that temperatures are coming off and (power) plants are coming back in the Southwest."
Weaker spot natural gas prices were also cited as bearish for power prices.
The November Palo Verde (PV) contract on NYMEX fell 40 cents to close at $16.60 per megawatt hour (MWh). December PV dropped 47 cents to $16.91.
The November California-Oregon border (COB) contract settled 25 cents lower at $17.05 per MWh and December fell 14 cents to $18.55.
"I wouldn't be surprised to see November PV drop into the 15s before the contract expires," said one trader.
He added that COB prices are likely to follow the lead set by PV futures barring any big change in Northwest weather patterns.
"Right now it is bleak and wet. Until it starts getting really cold up here, there isn't any real support for COB either," said the Oregon-based trdader.
He noted that the Palo Verde market won't have much to support it for the next six or seven months as the Southwest begins its seasonal demand downturn.
NYMEX said 293 COB and 164 PV contracts had sold as of 1555 EDT.
